Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Never drop not/never/no/only/except flip meaning worse than any token saved. Numbers, units exact.

Never ADD word to sound caveman. Compression only style never grow output. No inserted pronoun or copula to fake broken grammar: "when it not" cost one token more than "when not" and say same thing. Keep correct verb form when correct form cost same "sees" one token, "see" one token, so mangle buy nothing and read worse. Same rule as abbreviations and arrows: if caveman phrasing not shorter than plain phrasing, use plain.

Clarity register: mix ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English into caveman, always. One idea per sentence. Sentence short, target 20 words max. Active voice. Present tense where true. One word one meaning: same term for same thing every time, no synonym rotation. Instruction = imperative: "Run X", not "X should be run". Noun cluster 3 words max. Pronoun only with one clear referent, else repeat noun. Caveman cut filler; STE keep what make meaning unambiguous. Conflict between them → clarity win.

Tool calls: fire direct. No preamble, plan, or progress note before or between calls. After result: next call direct or final answer never announce next call. Text before call only to clarify, warn security/irreversible, or resolve ambiguity.

Follow explicit reply-language instructions from the user or project. Otherwise preserve the user's dominant language. Never switch because of example text or multilingual context elsewhere. Compress the style, not the language. Every emitted line in that language openings, pre-tool status lines, all not just final reply. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim unless user explicitly ask for translation.

'Drop articles' = article languages only. Where small markers carry case/role (particles, postpositions), keep them grammar, not filler; compress politeness/filler instead.

Answer directly in this style. Skip "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", "Caveman:" prefix or recap redundant with the reply itself. No normal answer plus caveman duplicate. User ask what mode is → say so plainly.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **ultra** | Strip conjunctions when cause-then-effect stay unambiguous. One word when one word enough. State each fact once. NO prose abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn/auth), NO arrows (X → Y) measured zero token saving under tokenizer, cost decode clarity. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never touch |

Example "Why React component re-render?"
- ultra: "Inline obj prop, new ref, re-render. `useMemo`."

Example "Explain database connection pooling."

Classical chars = wenyan modes only. Never swap a word to a classical char to shrink at non-wenyan levels.

- caveman:caveman-commit: Write a Conventional Commits message compressed to intent only. Use for "write a commit", "commit message", /commit or /caveman-commit.
- caveman:caveman-compress: Compress a memory file such as CLAUDE.md or a todo list into caveman format to save input tokens, keeping a readable backup. Trigger: /caveman-compress.
- caveman:caveman-discover: Find and label every LLM workflow in the repository so Caveman Cloud groups spend by workflow instead of one bucket. Use for "discover workflows" or breaking LLM spend down by workflow.

Use when asked to lower an agent's token cost, what caveman has saved, to trim a heavy CLAUDE.md, or to offload re-pasted context into cavemem.
- caveman:caveman-manage: Inspect Caveman Cloud's experiment lifecycle and block unsafe execution. Use when asked to start, approve, cancel, promote or roll back a Caveman experiment.
- caveman:caveman-optimize: Turn a Caveman optimization observation into an operator-chosen candidate with a paired baseline evaluation. Use when asked to inspect or evaluate a Caveman optimization report. Needs explicit approval.
- caveman:caveman-review: Compressed code review - one line per finding with location, problem and fix. Use for /caveman-review, "review this PR", or "review the diff".
- caveman:caveman-setup: Wire a repository through the Caveman Cloud gateway so every LLM request is measured, with no behavior change. Use for "set up caveman" or adding LLM spend observability.

- caveman:lean-build: Build feature work with high overbuilding risk. Use for new behavior, product slices, or integrations where repository reuse, strict scope, and an explicit stop condition matter.

- caveman:safe-refactor: Restructure code while preserving behavior. Use for extraction, consolidation, ownership moves, or cleanup where verification must bracket structural edits.
- caveman:surgical-patch: Fix bugs and small behavior changes at the narrowest responsible layer. Use when regression proof, preserved surrounding behavior, and task-relevant tests matter.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. "full" = final run; keep "test" until the user says otherwise ROOT = {"test": "data/inference_test/", "full": "data/inference/"}[RUN] # read references and write results only under ROOT METADATA = ROOT + "references/metadata.csv" # column dictionary: 1 row per RESULT column; type, unit, allowed values, trait code, definition, rule, example; ' | ' separates alternatives in allowed_values and example; the only format reference VALUE_MAP = ROOT + "references/value_map.csv" # paper terms and codes -> standard values for fire response, severity and resprouter type, with the notes entry to write MD_RAW = "data/papers_test/md_raw/*.md" # 2_pdf2md.py output, every PDF; last line "" or ""; Step 0 empties it PDF_CLEAN = "data/papers_test/pdf_clean/{stem}.pdf" # source PDF of each paper, renamed by 1_clean_pdf.py; same file stem as its markdown MD_LLM = "data/papers_test/md_llm/{stem}.md" # Step 0 output; one file per paper: optimised (scanned) or moved unchanged (text-layer, end comment "md_opt: none") PAPERS = "data/papers_test/md_llm/*.md" # extraction input; pages split by RESULT = ROOT + "results/{slug}.csv" # header = COLUMNS names, in COLUMNS order (39 columns) LOG = ROOT + "logs/{slug}_log.csv" # Step 1 log; header: paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS MD_LOG = ROOT + "logs/md_opt_log.csv" # Step 0 log; header: paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note + TOKEN_COLS TOKEN_COLS = "n_requests,input_tokens,cache_creation_input_tokens,cache_read_input_tokens,output_tokens,total_tokens" # last 6 log columns; agents leave them empty, USAGE fills them USAGE = "scripts/claude/usage.py" # token usage per paper; run by the user after each session, never by agents CHECK = "scripts/claude/check.py" # fixed check script; run it, never edit it; writes reports to ROOT + "logs/" ``` ## Read and write scope | Step | Read | Write | |---|---|---| | 0 | `MD_RAW`, `PDF_CLEAN` | `.md` files in `data/papers_test/md_llm/`; move or remove `.md` files in `data/papers_test/md_raw/`; `MD_LOG`; `CHECK --step0` report | | 1 | `METADATA`, `VALUE_MAP`, `PAPERS`, `RESULT`, `LOG` | `RESULT`, `LOG`; `CHECK` report | Everything not listed for a step is off limits for that step. One-off shell or Python commands are allowed; a code file may be written only to the session scratchpad (never to the repo), so its full text stays in the session transcript. ## Steps `print(...)` = write that status line to the chat as plain text, so the user can follow progress. `now_utc()` = output of `date -u +%FT%TZ`, e.g. `2026-10-02T08:04:26Z`. `bar(i, n)` = text progress bar, 20 characters wide: `[######--------------] 2/6 (33%)`. ```python # Step 0: optimise markdown. Only in a session where slug == MD_AGENT; other sessions never run Step 0. print(f"Step 0: optimise markdown | {len(MD_RAW)} papers") if not exists(MD_LOG): write(MD_LOG, "paper,status,pdf_pages,n_tables,n_fixes,unresolved,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS) for i, md in enumerate(sorted(MD_RAW), 1): out = MD_LLM(stem(md)) if exists(out) and out ends with "": # text-layer PDF: no optimisation move(md, out); replace(out, last line, "") log_md(stem(md), "text_layer", started=started, finished=now_utc()) print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | text_layer: moved unchanged"); continue pdf = PDF_CLEAN(stem(md)) # md ends with "" if not exists(pdf): # move md unchanged, add end comment with note move(md, out); replace(out, last line, ""); log_md(stem(md), "no_pdf", started=started, finished=now_utc(), note="no matching PDF") print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | no_pdf: moved unchanged"); continue print(f"{bar(i, len(MD_RAW))} {stem(md)} | {n_pages(pdf)} pages") for batch in pages(pdf, max_pages=10): # read PDF pages as images; never load a whole long PDF at once raw = text in md for the same pages # match by text on first and last page of batch; md may lack page markers append(out, optimise(raw, batch)) # see Markdown optimisation; append only, never overwrite earlier batches print(f" pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(pdf)} | tables rebuilt {n_tables}") append(out, "") log_md(stem(md), "done", n_pages(pdf), n_tables, n_fixes, unresolved, started, now_utc(), note) # 1 line per finished paper; quote cells with commas remove(md) # only after the end comment and MD_LOG line are written print(f" done | fixes {n_fixes} | unresolved {n_unresolved}") run(f"python {CHECK} --step0") # see Checks print(f"Step 0 done | {n_done} optimised, {n_text_layer} text_layer, {n_skipped} skipped") # Step 1: extract. One session per agent; this session handles only its own slug. Agents work independently. if MD_RAW is not empty: stop; tell the user to run Step 0 first print(f"Step 1: extract | agent {slug} | {len(PAPERS)} papers") if not exists(RESULT): write(RESULT, [name for name, rule in COLUMNS]) # header only write(LOG, "paper,status,n_rows,started,finished,note," + TOKEN_COLS) log("_run", "start", 0, now_utc(), "", f"model={AGENTS[slug]}; date=YYYY-MM-DD; git={git rev-parse HEAD}; claude_md_sha256=...; papers_sha256=...") # 1 line per run read(METADATA); read(VALUE_MAP) # column rules, value formats, term map for i, paper in enumerate(sorted(PAPERS), 1): # LC_ALL=C order; one paper at a time: finish its LOG line before starting the next if paper in LOG: # finished in an earlier run print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | skipped: in LOG"); continue started = now_utc() remove rows of paper from RESULT # leftovers from an interrupted run (match by `file_name`); state count in LOG note if broken(paper): # see Broken papers append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); log(paper, "broken", 1, started, now_utc(), reason) print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | broken: {reason}"); check_paper(paper); continue print(f"{bar(i, len(PAPERS))} {stem(paper)} | {n_pages(paper)} pages") for batch in pages(paper, max_pages=10): # never load a whole long paper at once append(RESULT, extract(batch)) # write after every batch print(f" pages {first}-{last} of {n_pages(paper)} | rows {n_rows}") if n_rows == 0: # readable, but no relevant data append(RESULT, na_row(paper, reason)); log(paper, "no_data", 1, started, now_utc(), reason) print(f" no_data: {reason}"); check_paper(paper); continue log(paper, "done", n_rows, started, now_utc(), problems) print(f" done | rows {n_rows} | problems {len(problems)}") check_paper(paper) print(f"Checks | agent {slug} | all papers") run(f"python {CHECK} {slug}") # see Checks print(f"Step 1 done | agent {slug} | papers {n_done} done, {n_broken} broken, {n_no_data} no_data | rows {total_rows} | failed checks {n_failed}") ``` Hashes, run from the repo root, exactly: `papers_sha256` = `sha256sum data/papers_test/md_llm/*.md | LC_ALL=C sort | sha256sum`; `claude_md_sha256` = `sha256sum CLAUDE.md`. Record the first 64 characters of the output. Tokens: never estimate. Leave the 6 `TOKEN_COLS` cells empty on every log line; record `started` and `finished` for every paper (`USAGE` uses them). ## Markdown optimisation Compare each scanned paper's `MD_RAW` file with its PDF page by page. Fix the markdown so it matches the PDF. Raw text of a scanned PDF may be poor OCR or empty (no text layer): then build each page from the PDF page image. Do not copy the `` line into `MD_LLM`. - Tables: rebuild every table as a markdown pipe table, one species per row, values in the correct column. Fix rows split by wrapped species names, merged cells (`
` lists), and multi-line headers spread over several rows. Read tables from the PDF page, not from the broken markdown. - Text: fix split ligatures (`fi re` -> `fire`, `fl ower` -> `flower`), OCR errors (`Brishane` -> `Brisbane`), joined words, and scrambled word order. - Remove conversion junk: `` tags, stray OCR lines, and the `{N}` prefix before page markers. - Put exactly one `` between PDF pages. Add markers where missing (OCR output has none). - Keep all content, including title, authors, abstract, and references. Do not summarise, reorder sections, or add text that is not in the PDF. - Value unreadable in the PDF: keep it as printed and list it under `unresolved` in the end comment. Table that cannot be rebuilt: list it as `unresolved=table N`. ## Extraction rules - One row per species × study site × fire. Same species at two sites, or two fires at one site = two rows. - Use only text in the paper. No background knowledge. No estimates. - Value not stated in paper: leave cell empty. - Species tables often span many pages. Read every page; extract every species row. - Table continues into the next batch: reuse its column headers from the previous batch. - Carry site and fire values (coordinates, location name, rainfall, fire season, severity, type) from the paper's methods onto every row of that paper. Several sites or fires: match each species row to its own site and fire. - Several named sites share one set of coordinates: still 1 row per site; site name in `location_name`, coordinates kept. Never merge sites into 1 row with per-site values in `notes`. - A row needs at least 1 value in a fire response or time column. Values kept only in `notes` (near-matches, unreliable or unitless values) never create a row on their own. Exception: a fire response code left out of the cell by a `VALUE_MAP` rule (no clear class, conflicting codes) still creates a row. - Value given once for several sites (not split by site): the species recorded at 1 of those sites only -> value on that site's row. Recorded at 2 or more -> 1 extra row with `location_name` = those site names joined by `; `, coordinates empty; site-specific values stay on the site rows. Never put a shared value on one site's row when the species is recorded at several sites. - Never merge rows. Same taxon printed as 2 or more separate entries (e.g. different references or variants): 1 row per entry. Duplicate rows are fine; do not check or remove them. - Fill a column only when the paper's measure matches the column definition. Near-matches go in `notes` only, with their definition (e.g. time to 80% of maximum flower production; expert or literature estimates). - Not yet flowering at the last observation ("not flowering after 4 years"): `>N`, e.g. `>4`. - Codes and units: use only definitions printed in the paper. Code not defined: copy it as printed (e.g. fire response `S`), never translate it. Unit not stated for a time value: leave the time columns empty; value and "unit not stated" in `notes`. - Tables may be parsed with one-off code. Then print 3 random parsed rows next to their source table lines and confirm they match before writing them. - Ambiguous value: fill best reading, explain in `notes`. Value printed with uncertainty marks (`c.`, `?`, `approx.`): fill the number without the marks; marks in `notes`. - Every place named in `data_location` gets its verbatim quote in `data_quote`: the sentence, the species' table row, or the figure label and title (see `METADATA`). Copy it from the paper's markdown, not from memory; `CHECK` searches the paper for it. - Ambiguous column (paper does not say which measure a value is, e.g. not stated whether from seed or from resprouts): `notes` only. - Several estimates of one measure for the same species, site and fire (e.g. pooled model in a table and a single-site model in the text): fill the value from the paper's main results table; the others in `notes`. ## Broken papers and papers without data Every paper gets at least 1 row in `RESULT`. Write an NA row when: - **broken**: file empty or under 1,000 bytes; no `` and runs Step 0 for it. - **no_data**: paper readable, all pages read, no species-level juvenile period or fire response values found. ```python na_row = {name: "NA" for name, rule in COLUMNS} # exactly 1 NA row per paper na_row["notes"] = reason # e.g. "empty markdown: PDF conversion failed"; "no data: review paper, no species values" na_row["source"] = citation if readable else stem(paper) na_row["file_name"] = stem(paper) na_row["pdf_path"] = pdf_path(paper) # see METADATA na_row["supplementary_material"] = items if any else "NA" # see Supplementary material ``` Paper breaks partway: keep rows already extracted, add the 1 NA row, continue with next paper. Supplementary material (not in `PAPERS`): paper refers to supplementary or supporting material, or to items such as `Table S1`, `Appendix S2`, `Online Resource 1` -> fill `supplementary_material` on every row of that paper, NA row included (see `METADATA`). Extract what the main text gives; never guess the supplement's values. ## Columns Order in `RESULT`, grouped by similarity. Names = the existing dataset's names after `janitor::clean_names()` (lower case, `_` for spaces, `%` -> `percent`); `new` = column not in it. Each column's definition, unit, allowed values, fill rule and example are in `METADATA` (same names, same order); follow them as part of these rules. ```python COLUMNS = [ # taxon ("genus", ""), ("species", ""), ("subsp", ""), ("scientific_name", ""), ("native_status", "new"), ("family", ""), # fire response ("fire_response_categorical_surv1", ""), ("fire_response_implied", "new"), ("resprouter_type", ""), # time after fire ("pjp_mths", ""), ("primary_juvenile_period", ""), ("age_at_first_flower_production_from_seed_repr3", ""), ("secondary_juvenile_period", ""), ("time_to_first_flower_production_resprout_repr3a", ""), ("time_to_50_percent_flowering_repr4", ""), ("time_to_50_percent_flowering", "new"), ("time_to_80_percent_flowering", "new"), ("recovery_time", "new"), ("time_unit", "new"), # error of a time value ("error_column", "new"), ("error_type", "new"), ("error_value", "new"), ("sample_size", "new"), # site ("location_name", "new"), ("latitude", ""), ("longitude", ""), ("rainfall_mm", ""), ("rainfall_post_fire_mm", "new"), ("rainfall_post_fire_period", "new"), # fire ("fire_type", "new"), ("fire_season_categorical", ""), ("fire_severity_categorical", ""), # record ("data_location", "new"), ("data_quote", "new"), ("supplementary_material", "new"), ("notes", ""), ("source", ""), ("file_name", "new"), ("pdf_path", "new"), ] ``` Time columns: - Fixed-unit column (`METADATA` unit = months or years), value reported in another unit: convert to the column's unit (years = months / 12 = weeks / 52 = days / 365; months = weeks / 4.33 = days / 30.4); write ` converted from N ` in `notes`. No other conversion. - Paper gives values under different terms (e.g. age at first flowering and primary juvenile period): each value in its own column. Apart from the `pjp_mths` rule in `METADATA`, one value never fills 2 columns. - Precision: copy values with exactly the decimals printed in the paper. Do not round or add trailing zeros (`3.0` stays `3.0`; `3` stays `3`). Converted value: paper or source states the value in the target unit -> copy it as printed. Otherwise round to 3 decimals, drop trailing zeros (26 months -> 2.167; 30 months -> 2.5; 48 months -> 4). - Ranges: `min-max`, no spaces (`3.0 - 16.0` -> `3.0-16.0`). Open bounds as printed (`>23`, `<2`). Uncertain value: no `?` in the cell; explain in `notes`. CSV format: UTF-8, comma separator, LF line endings, decimal point `.`. Quote any cell containing a comma, quote, or newline; double inner quotes. Empty cell = no value; `NA` only in NA rows. Trim leading and trailing spaces in every cell. Case: lower case in every cell (`Myrtaceae` -> `myrtaceae`, `Summer` -> `summer`, author and place names too), except: first letter of `genus` (also in `scientific_name`); `NA`; codes copied as printed, in any column including `notes` (case can carry meaning, e.g. `R` vs `r`); `file_name` (= file stem, also in `source` when used there); `data_quote` (verbatim from the paper); `pdf_path` (file path as on disk). Several values in one cell: separate with `; ` (semicolon, space), e.g. `autumn; spring`; a `/` printed inside a single value (e.g. code `K/r`, a site name) stays as printed. Dashes: ASCII hyphen `-` in every cell except `data_quote`, including names, codes and `source` (en dash `–` or em dash `—` -> `-`). Form not set by a rule: use the form of the `METADATA` example. Uncertain value: keep the format; explain in `notes`. ## Checks `CHECK` tests the format rules that need no reading of the paper. It prints a summary, writes a report to `ROOT + "logs/"`, and exits 1 if any error is found. ```python def check_paper(paper): # after every paper's LOG line, including broken and no_data; never skip for attempt in 1..3: if run(f"python {CHECK} {slug} --paper '{stem(paper)}'") == 0: return fix each failed row from the paper; fix LOG n_rows if rows changed log the remaining errors in the paper's LOG note ``` After all papers: run `CHECK` without `--paper`, fix errors the same way. After Step 0: run `CHECK --step0`, fix each failed `MD_LLM` file from its PDF. Warnings: look, fix if real. Never delete a row silently. ## Do not - Read `data/reference/`, `data/papers_test/answers/`, `logs/benchmark*.csv`, or another agent's `RESULT` or `LOG`. They contain answers. - Edit `METADATA`, `VALUE_MAP`, `PDF_CLEAN`, or anything in `data/papers_test/` outside `md_raw/` (Step 0 only: move or remove) and `md_llm/`. - Edit `CHECK`, or write any script file outside the session scratchpad. - Create or write anything in `data/inference/`. Use `data/inference_test/` only.

- [Always log pipeline runs](always-log-pipeline-runs.md) — every Step 0/1 session: snapshot, sessions.csv, tokens via SessionEnd hook
- [Rule refinement goal](rule-refinement-goal.md) — accuracy first (meta-analysis), same format across models second; content differences OK
- [Answer key fix pending](answer-key-fix-pending.md) — user fixing ground truth (2026-10-09); rescore, clear old outputs, offer row-override rule
- [Pipeline roadmap](pipeline-roadmap.md) — after ground truth: rescore, pydantic validate.py, then locator/quote/review queue (human review is part of pipeline; fast checking is the goal)
- [User does git](user-does-git.md) — never commit or push; user commits themselves
